description: This case study is Ofgem's final report on the review into how electricity distribution network operators responded to Storm Arwen, published on 9 June 2022 in 49 pages, after an interim report in February 2022. It reports that over one million customers lost power, about 40,000 for more than three days and nearly 4,000 for over a week, and assesses network resilience (overhead line poles, tree cutting), planning and winter preparedness, handling of incidents, communication and post-incident support. The executive summary records payments of an extra 10.28 million pounds to consumer resilience funds by three operators on top of 29.64 million pounds of compensation, and a possible licence breach over a call centre. Access: free PDF from Ofgem; no licence is stated in the text read. Coverage is Great Britain distribution networks. Caveats: only the contents and executive summary were read here, and Ofgem focuses on licence compliance, not engineering causes. It suits resilience and emergency response studies of storm restoration and regulation, and it relates to the government review record catalogued here as case_study-e3c-storm-arwen-review-final-report-2022.

name: Ofgem final report on the review into the networks' response to Storm Arwen (June 2022)
outcomes: Over one million customers lost power; about 40,000 were off supply for more than three days and nearly 4,000 for over a week. Three network operators agreed to pay an extra 10.28 million pounds to consumer resilience funds on top of 29.64 million pounds already paid in compensation, and two agreed to spend 3.7 and 1.2 million pounds on network resilience; one operator accepted its call centre fell short of its licence obligations. The chapters cover overhead line poles, tree cutting, winter preparedness, fault management, resource deployment, mutual aid, generators, contact centres, restoration time estimates and compensation.
provider: Ofgem (Office of Gas and Electricity Markets)
